What's Stored on a Prepper Disk
Reference
Wikipedia (English)
Over 6 million articles and images. Searchable and browsable just like the real site.
WikiHow
90,000+ how-to guides, from finding shelter to wiring a house.
iFixit Repair Guides
Professional-grade repair instructions for autos, electronics, and home appliances.
Project Gutenberg
60,000 eBooks across 300+ categories — classics, non-fiction, children's books, and more.
TED Talks
Curated videos on farming and extreme weather.
Stack Exchange Q&A
Thousands of searchable questions on sustainable living and the outdoors.
Khan Academy Lite
Hundreds of video lessons and quizzes on Math, Biology, History, Computer Programming, and more. Store and track your progress on your Prepper Disk.
Crisis Response
Ready.gov / FEMA
Disaster planning for biohazards, weather events, mass attacks, home fires, and more.
Medical Wikis & Guides
50,000+ articles from the National Library of Medicine, MedlinePlus, and surgical/first-aid guides.
Survival Bookshelf
Military survival manuals, hunting and trapping, foraging, post-disaster cooking.
Ky Furneaux Field Guides
Fortifying your home, finding water, signaling, rescue — from the survival expert (Discovery, MTV).
Prepper Disk Exclusives
Original eBooks: livestock for survival, woodland survival, emergency communication.

World Street Maps
North America, Europe, and Oceania street maps with satellite imagery.
National Park MapsNEW
Official trail maps for all 63 US National Parks.

Now it's up to you. What do you do?
#1 You leave this page

This is not for you, so you decide not to get a Prepper Disk. Maybe you don’t believe information is vital. Or you do and you have volumes of books, guides, and maps already. But you don't need a digital backup in case of fire, or “pocket library” for when you need to abandon your house within 5 minutes because it’s about to be flooded.

Or maybe it’s too expensive? Then send us an email here and we’ll see what we can do.

#2 You'll DIY your own Prepper Disk

Building a Prepper Disk yourself is doable. All you need is a Raspberry Pi, a durable case, all of the information on it which will take weeks to collect and download, build a UI, and then hope it all works smoothly.

Yes, it's doable for sure. I've done it myself, and if you want a challenging DIY project, go for it.

To be honest, it's a fun project, but it took me a tremendous amount of effort and troubleshooting to get the setup right, and the hours and frustration involved aren't really for everyone.

#3 You go for convenience, speed, and peace of mind
